problem: Audio-visual navigation work targets single sound-source scenarios, and the only audio dataset (SAVi) has one clip per category (144 clips, about 1,157 s). It cannot simulate diverse multi-source or noisy scenes, and existing methods degrade sharply when interfering sounds and background noise are present.
motivation: Real homes contain several simultaneous sounds (TV, traffic, appliances), and the agent must pick out the target sound and track it even when it goes silent. Without a large and diverse audio set and a framework that handles multiple sources, audio-visual navigation cannot move toward real deployment.
key_idea: Build a large sound-event dataset (BeDAViN) to simulate multi-source and noisy scenes, and propose ENMuS3, which uses a sound event descriptor (class-wise category and DoA estimation smoothed by an LSTM) plus a multi-scale scene memory transformer to locate and track the target sound.
insight: Gains are largest in single-source and multi-source scenes (SR +13.1 and +7.1 over the best baseline) and shrink under heavy background noise (+3.1, absolute SR only 18.0), so noise remains the hard case. The paper attributes the SR gains to the sound event descriptor and the SPL/SNA gains to the multi-scale memory transformer. However, the component ablations are only in the supplementary material and are not in the main text, so this attribution is not directly verified here.
method: BeDAViN dataset: 2,258 clips (10.8 h) covering 20 target sound categories and 4 noise categories (rain, bird, traffic, fireworks). It combines 158 manual binaural recordings with clips from AudioSet, FSD50K and freesound.org, and provides 1.5M/3k/3k train/val/test episodes over 85 Matterport3D scenes.
Audio encoder: binaural STFT gives a 4-channel feature (left and right real parts, IPD, ILD), which a CRNN encodes into a low-level audio embedding.

Sound event descriptor: predicts class-wise 3D DoA vectors, marks a class active if the vector norm is at least 0.5, converts DoAs to global yaw/pitch, and feeds the last Nd steps to an LSTM whose hidden state is the high-level audio embedding.
Observation encoders and scene memory: a ResNet visual encoder plus linear pose and action encoders. The concatenated embedding is stored in a FIFO memory of the last Nm observations.

Multi-scale scene memory transformer: stacked convolutions with the same kernel size and stride build a multi-resolution memory. The decoder combines a convolution branch for local features of the current observation with a cross-attention branch for global memory interactions, followed by an actor-critic head.
Simulation: SoundSpaces is modified to add interfering-sound and background-noise generation. It defines single-source, multi-source and noisy scenarios.

setting.backbone: ENMuS3: CRNN audio encoder + LSTM descriptor + ResNet + multi-scale scene memory transformer + actor-critic (RL, trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: 1.5M navigation episodes on BeDAViN across 85 Matterport3D scenes
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D (128x128) + binaural audio (16 kHz) + pose
setting.action_space: low-level discrete actions (move forward, turn left, turn right, stop)

numbers_note: Only Table 2 gives results. The ablations are in the supplementary material, which is not included. The split is 'test' with a subset of 10 scenes x 100 episodes.
results: ENMuS3 beats all baselines on BeDAViN in every scenario. SR is 79.3 / 46.5 / 18.0 for single-source / multi-source / noisy, versus 66.3 / 37.9 / 14.1 for the strongest baseline, SMT+Audio. The gains are also seen in SPL, SNA and DTG.
limitations: Absolute success in noisy scenarios is low (SR 18.0) and the gain over the best baseline is small (+3.1).
Evaluated only in simulation on 10 scenes x 100 episodes, with no real-robot experiments, and the ablations are only in the supplementary material.
Sounds are simulated using clips recorded within 1 m, which may not reflect real acoustic conditions.
